summary: AAA Band's ZX Spectrum megademo, shown here in its party version, which came second in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at DiHalt 2014 Lite. It was made by a large crew of coders, artists and musicians.
why: A runner-up at DiHalt 2014 Lite that pulls together work from around a dozen Spectrum sceners, including code from Rob F, g0blinish, Trefi and SerzhSoft and music by Rob F, Splinter and nq.
highlights: graphics by Mellone, Lee and AAA

summary: A Commodore 64 intro by Digital Sounds System, with code by Street Tuff and graphics by Knoeki, that came 7th in the Alternative Platforms compo at Evoke 2012. The video is live footage from the party hall.
why: A small, informal party release that shows up at a big PC-oriented party's alternative platforms compo. Worth a look for the C64 side of Evoke 2012.

summary: Genesis Project's 2014 C64 demo presenting a new Rob Hubbard tune, "New Frontier", produced as a SID with Max Hall for the film From Bedrooms to Billions, with Redcrab's caricature of Hubbard at the piano.
why: Rob Hubbard's first new C64 music in decades. Sceners single out the full-length tune's Hubbard-style bassline and lead slides, and even those cooler on the music praise Redcrab's graphics.

quote.text: such an excellent tune, building and building towards multiple climaxes. super it's not just a short ditty, but a truly full length composition.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo coded by Acid Maker and Scorpio with music by Jakub Husak, which won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k21 WE.
why: It took first place in the Spectrum demo competition at Silly Venture 2k21 WE, one of the main parties for 8-bit platforms.

summary: Genesis Project's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Gubbdata 2020, built around a single idea: everything on screen runs on the diagonal. Code by Shadow, graphics by Facet, music by Stinsen.
why: Sceners praise how consistently the diagonal theme is carried through, along with Facet's pictures and Stinsen's soundtrack, which several single out as the highlight.

quote.text: Love the idea of this demo. Everything is diagonal. Excellent pictures. I can listen to the music the whole day, and I probably will.

summary: A 256-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit by Szeryf, which won the Atari XL/XE 256b intro compo at Silly Venture 2k23 WE. Filmed on real hardware.
why: It took first place in its size category at Silly Venture, one of the main Atari 8-bit parties.
highlights: car driving past a dotted skyline

summary: A 254-byte Atari 8-bit intro by JAC!, who handled both code and music. It placed 4th in the Atari ST/800XL Demo/Bootsector compo at Outline 2011.
why: A small-size production that fits code and music into 254 bytes, with its source released. It's worth a look for what a single coder squeezed into so few bytes.

summary: A C64 4K intro by Ancients Pledge, with music by NecroPolo, that won the 8-bit demo compo at Euskal 2010. Wireframe objects spin in a grey panel, framed by coloured boxes that echo the lines.
why: A 4K intro that beat full-size entries in the 8-bit demo compo at Euskal 2010. Sceners singled out its screen design and the maze effect.

quote.text: I liked the screen design and maze effect

summary: Taboo's C64 demo from the end of 1992, which won the C64 demo compo at Skylight Party. Code by K.M. and MMS, graphics by Shaman and Wayne, running to roughly half an hour of parts.
why: Sceners single out the plot scroller, with Shadow calling it probably the best on the C64, along with the morphing vectors, raytraced ball and music selection. Some find it slow. It was voted 12th best demo in Design #1 in 1997.

quote.text: But the plot-scroller, wow, probably the best I have seen on the C64, and in the border even for that extra little spice.

summary: A preview of Trilobit's Atari 2600 demo Triptych, coded by visy and Ilmarque, with music and graphics by Ilmarque. It placed third in the Oldschool Demo compo at Stream 2009.
why: A third place at Stream 2009 for a VCS demo, made by a two-person team where Ilmarque handled code, music and graphics.

summary: Dekadence's beer-themed C64 demo, placed 3rd in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2001. Code, graphics and music by BriteLite, with graphics from Spiikki and music from SounDemoN.
why: Sceners single out its unusual look and atmosphere, the colour choices and the wild, fast music. A review on c64.sk called it plasma-like effects with decent black and white graphics on top, timed to the music.

quote.text: it's totally out there, great theme and colour choice, wild music, very unique demo. has an awesome look to it.

summary: Party Bit 25% is a Commodore 64 demo by Ate Bit (the video also credits Hack'n'Trade). It came 3rd in the Oldskool Demo compo at Sundown 2013.
why: It is a rare C64 demo written for three SID chips, and it placed in the Sundown 2013 oldskool demo compo.

summary: Chorus's C64 demo that won the demo compo at Árok 2005, shown there as a preview and released once finished: an old-school run of parts with code by Clarence, graphics by Leon and music by DRAX, plus a note file.
why: Sceners liked its old-school feel and subtle but effective effects, singling out the 10-sprites-per-line tricks in the lower border and note file, the soundtrack and the simple final part.

quote.text: I really enjoyed this demo and the final part was actually my favourite. So simple but effective. Just beautiful! Lovely tunes as well!

summary: Arise's C64 demo, a sequel, that won the demo competition at North Party 2002. It includes Katon's fullscreen picture Final Fight, which won the graphics compo at the same party.
why: Sceners praise its inventive effects and the care taken over design and transitions. Several call it one of the best C64 demos of its decade, and it is still on many favourite lists.

quote.text: One of the most creative, best designed and most impressively coded demos ever made. Pointy hat off.

summary: A 4K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Praline, Pulpo Corrosivo and Arkos, coded by Toms with graphics by Barjack and music by Targhan. It placed third in the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision Online 2020.
why: A podium finish in a competitive oldskool 4K compo at Revision, packing hand-drawn character sprites and a tracked tune into four kilobytes, compressed with Shrinkler.

summary: sibCrew's ZX Spectrum 128K demo, coded by wbcbz7 and Denis Grachev with music by Nik-O, which won the LowEnd Demo compo at DiHalt 2017.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2017, beating the rest of the LowEnd demo field on home ground for Spectrum sceners.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Cyberpunks Unity that won the 8-bit 640k demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2006, with code by Alff and Elfh and music by Simon.
why: It took first place in its compo at Chaos Constructions 2006, one of the main Russian scene parties for Spectrum work.
highlights: colourful full-screen effect under the logo

summary: A 1K intro by Alone Coder for an enhanced ZX Spectrum, which won the Combined 8-Bit 1024b Intro compo at DiHalt 2013.
why: It took first place in a combined 8-bit 1K compo at DiHalt 2013, beating entries from other 8-bit platforms within a 1024-byte limit.

summary: Nah-Kolor's four-disk-side C64 demo, made with a large cast of guest coders, graphicians and musicians, that placed 5th in the demo compo at X 2023. This is the party version; Multiverse 100% followed at X 2024.
why: Nominated for Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2024. Sceners single out the 'comafight' fighting sequence, the fake ending with more demo after it, the plasma zoomers and the homages to Censor, Booze and Fossil.
highlights: fake end and hidden extra demo

quote.text: What a behemoth! Lovely and well-crafted by a super-talented team. I really liked the fighting sequence, super well done.

summary: Black Box's Game Boy Color demo, placed 4th in the Console/Handheld compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2004, with code by Credo and Merlin, music by Fusion and full-screen artwork from guest artists.
why: A Game Boy Color demo that brought in guest artists Enok/Exceed, Poison/Singular Crew and Angelday for its full-screen pictures and logos.

summary: A C64 demo by Prosonix and Offence with an alien theme, placed 8th in the demo compo at X 2016. Pal's pictures include a Trump portrait and an alien band playing beside a crashed saucer.
why: Sceners single out Pal's pixel art and the music, and note how much content was built in about five weeks, much of it coded at the party. Effects built from letters and words also get mentions.

quote.text: The alien concert suddenly materializing near the wrecked soucer was the coolest surprise I've seen in a long time. Such great pixel art too.

summary: A C64 4K intro by 4mat and Street Tuff, released in June 2010 during the World Cup: a silhouetted vuvuzela player against the South African flag, with SID sound imitating the horn's drone.
why: A topical joke that landed well. Sceners laughed at how convincingly the SID recreates the vuvuzela, and one likened it to something the 1986 scene would have made.

quote.text: Extremely authentic--it feels like exactly the sort of thing the scene circa 1986 could and would have done.

summary: Joker's 8K ZX Spectrum intro, coded by Dalthon with music by MCH and Pator, which won the ZX Spectrum Intro compo at Xenium 2022. Its original idea is credited to Luke and Wacek.
why: It took first place in the Spectrum intro compo at Xenium 2022. The video is a live recording from the party hall.

summary: Synergy 2 is an Amstrad CPC demo by Impact from 2008, with code by CMP, graphics by BDC Iron and music by Tom&Jerry. Grim linked it and built a cheat part with Supersly and PulkoMandy.
why: A CPC group production with a hidden cheat part that has its own 32K picture and a PulkoMandy cover of a Jonathan Dunn tune.

summary: A C64 4K intro by Resource, coded by Bubis and Edhellon with music by guest artist Jeff, that came second in the C64 4K Intro compo at Breakpoint 2010.
why: Sceners praise its single effect for its real sense of depth, and say Jeff's tune suits it well. Fitting it into 4K drew credit too.

quote.text: Nice effect, a real sense of depth and the tune suits it well.

summary: Bandwagon's MSX demo from 1998, which won the wild compo at Zoo 1998.
why: A compo winner at Zoo 1998 and well regarded on Pouët, it's a good example of what the MSX scene was doing in the late 1990s.

summary: Triad's minimal, concept-driven C64 demo that came second in the C64 demo compo at Little Computer People 2004: slow, text-free abstract visuals set to ambient music.
why: Sceners praise its calm tempo and restrained design, several saying it should have won the compo. Some found the parts overlong, but many describe it as something to drift away to.

quote.text: I love the calm tempo, it takes a lot of your attention. Its just like listening to the rain or experience a sunset over an open sea.

summary: A 4K intro for the Atari VCS by Tjoppen, who also wrote the code. It placed 9th in the Alternative Platforms compo at Evoke 2012.
why: A one-person 4K production on the Atari 2600, one of the most constrained machines in the scene, shown at a major German party's alternative-platforms competition.

summary: A small Atari 2600 demo by Noice, coded by Shadow with music by Jakub Husak. It came 6th in the Atari 8-bit Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k10.
why: A rare VCS entry in an Atari 8-bit demo compo, worth a look for what Shadow squeezed out of the 2600 at Silly Venture 2010.

summary: Reflex's C64 demo, placed third in the Wild compo at Revision 2025. You plug the audio and video cables in the wrong way round, so the SID makes the picture and the video chip makes the sound.
why: Nominated for Outstanding Concept at The Meteoriks 2026. Sceners praise it as a simple idea with a lot of complexity underneath, and single out the smooth greyscales, the raster effects and the sample at the end.

quote.text: Still the exact same hardware, but a completely new result that feels alien, maybe from near a black hole where the laws of physics don't apply.

summary: Defence Force's Oric demo, also known as the VIP4 demo, which won the Oldschool Demo compo at Very Important Party 2002. A group effort with code by Jede, Twilighte and Dbug and graphics from several artists.
why: It took first place in the Oldschool Demo compo at Very Important Party 2002, and it brings together a large part of the Oric scene's coders and artists in one production.

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo by Dirty Minds, coded by Optimus with music by Aki, that won the CPC Demo compo at Forever 2006.
why: It took first place in the CPC demo competition at Forever 2006, a good example of mid-2000s CPC coding from Optimus.

summary: A Commodore 64 1K intro by 4mat, released under the Ate Bit name, that won the Commodore 1K Intro compo at Forever 2007 (Forever 8).
why: Sceners were struck by how much fits in 1K, singling out the music and its use of samples. One later viewer still wondered how it could even have digis at that size.

quote.text: How the heck is this 1k? Awesome! It even has digis!

summary: Lethargy's two-disk-side Commodore 64 demo, released for the group's anniversary, which won the demo compo at Árok 2021. Code by Visage, Ego, Strepto and others, graphics by Grass, Poison and Leon, music by Vincenzo.
why: Sceners single out Vincenzo's soundtrack, the graphics in the vertical megascroller, the tunnel and a funny end part, along with the bitmap scroller of famous scene names and logos at the start.

quote.text: the gfx in the vertical megascroller rule and the tunnel is awesome. endpart is funny for sure.

summary: Cycleburner's C64 4K intro, second in the 4K Intro compo at X 2023: a minimalist show built around numbers counting through screen memory locations, with a cursor block wandering the screen and out into the border.
why: Sceners single out the original concept and its humour, a clever idea carried through with lots of small details in a very sparse presentation. Many named it a favourite of the party.

quote.text: There's so many clever details with such a minimalistic presentation. It all comes together as very entertaining show, I love it!

summary: Padua's single-file C64 demo, coded by LHS with music by PCH and Sad, which won the Commodore Demo compo at Forever 2008.
why: Sceners note how much is crammed into one file, and single out the 512-dot rotating teapot, the filled vector show and PCH's tune in the second half. Some found the frame rate slow.

quote.text: Really entertaining, and neat design too. I like it a lot.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by bfox that placed 2nd in the 8 Bit Intro 256b compo at Multimatograf 2017.
why: A second place at Multimatograf for an intro that fits sound as well as visuals into 256 bytes.
highlights: pulsing bars like a level meter

summary: Atari 2600 demo by Onslaught and Disaster Area, with code by Krion, graphics by Almighty God and music by cTrix. It won the oldschool demo compo at Flashback 2019.
why: A compo winner at Flashback 2019 on one of the most restrictive machines a demo can target. The video is a real-hardware PAL capture.

summary: Hooy-Program's ZX Spectrum 48K demo, made entirely by Gasman (code, graphics and AY music), which won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2006.
why: A first place at Forever 2006 from a one-person effort, with Gasman handling every part of the production himself. It runs on a stock 48K machine.

summary: sibCrew's ZX Spectrum demo, second in the 8 Bit Demo compo at Multimatograf 2017, with code by Denchik, graphics by rook and music by Olezhik.
why: A podium finish at Multimatograf 2017 from the Siberian group, with a large team credited for code, graphics, ASCII art and music.
highlights: "To LDIR or not to LDIR" screen

summary: Silicon Limited's C64 demo, coded and scored by Scout with graphics by Tim, which came second in the demo compo at Primary Star 2005.
why: A comeback release, reportedly made in three weeks after years of silence. Sceners single out its style, smooth transitions, funky graphics and Scout's tune.

quote.text: Slick. It's got style, it's got great transitions. Made me happy.

summary: Tristar and Red Sector Inc.'s demo for the Commodore 64 DTV, a picture shown in a new 1280-colour interlaced graphics mode with a scroller over it. It came second in the combined demo/intro compo at Nordlicht 2012.
why: Sceners who saw it on real hardware were struck by how the new mode removes almost all the flicker of standard interlace, and by the transparent scroller.

quote.text: i saw the standard interlace version which flickered pretty good and this new mode which manages to remove the flickering almost completely.

summary: Fatzone's Commodore 64 demo, second in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2011.
why: Sceners called it one of the pleasant surprises of the compo and a clear step up from Fatzone's earlier work. The waves, twister and diagonal bars get singled out.

quote.text: a nice surprise during the compo, neat stuff. enjoyed it.

summary: Kowalski's 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro with sound, which won the 8 Bit Intro 256b compo at Multimatograf 2017.
why: A compo winner in the 256-byte category at Multimatograf 2017, and one of the size-limited intros that manages sound as well as visuals.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by mayHem, Alone Coder and Hooy-Program for the ATM Turbo 2 clone, recorded on ZX Evolution with NeoGS sound. It came second in the demo compo at ZX AAA Compo 2013.
why: A runner-up at ZX AAA Compo 2013 that targets the Russian ATM Turbo 2 clone rather than a stock Spectrum, with music by Yerzmyey on the General Sound card. The scroller notes it was the group's first demo with GS music.

summary: An Amstrad CPC 4K intro by Pulpo Corrosivo, with code and graphics by Toms and music by Tom et Jerry. It placed 4th in the Oldskool 4k Intro compo at Revision 2023.
why: It made the Meteoriks 2024 watchlist, a sign it stood out among that year's releases despite its modest compo placing.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128 demo by Darklite and Offence, with code by Neon, graphics by Pal, music by Response and text by tFt. It shared second place in the Combined Real-Time compo at Black Valley 2023.
why: A party scroller from two groups working together. It tied for second place in the combined real-time compo at Black Valley 2023.

summary: Ate Bit's ZX Spectrum demo, placed third in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2006, with code and graphics by evilpaul, more graphics from Eater and Rudsy, and music by 4mat.
why: A podium finish at Forever 2006 from a small team, with three credited graphicians, which shows in the mix of bold blocky shapes and detailed pictures.

summary: A 256-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit by Agenda, coded by Svoy, which placed third in the Atari XL/XE 256b intro compo at Silly Venture 2k18.
why: A podium finish in a crowded size-limited compo at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party, from a 256-byte program.

summary: A short C64 demo by Panda Design, with code and music by radiantx and graphics by Frost, that placed third in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2010.
why: Sceners praise its stylish design, Frost's graphics and especially radiantx's drum-and-bass soundtrack. The overlay-patterns screen gets singled out, though many wished it ran longer.

quote.text: The first "screen" is amazing. Great gfx through the whole demo and very stylish along with a nice soundtrack.
